[[File:Decipher.com Hoth Contest page 1996.jpg|thumb|Hoth Contest, November 1996.]]
[[File:Decipher.com Dagobah Contest page 1997.jpg|thumb|The Dagobah Contest, March 1997.]]
[[Decipher.com]] ran online contests for the [[Star Wars CCG]] from 1996, including daily card-title puzzles, website Easter egg hunts and fan design contests.

== Hoth Contest (1996) ==
The 1996 Hoth Contest posted a daily anagram of a preview card's title.<ref>[http://games.decipher.com/hothcontest/index.html Hoth Contest], Decipher (1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961102055122/http://games.decipher.com/hothcontest/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> A wind sound file played on the contest page.

Recovered daily pages include:

== Easter Egg Hunt (1997) ==
The ''What's New'' area (<code>/new/</code>) ran the Decipher Easter Egg Hunt, with one egg hidden on the website each weekday from 21 to 31 March 1997.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/new/easteregghunt97/index.html The Decipher Easter Egg Hunt 1997], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327205157/http://www.decipher.com:80/new/easteregghunt97/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> The Hoth Easter egg hunt closed on 19 December 1997 with two eggs never found.<ref>[http://decipher.com/insidedecipher/archives/1997/hothcontestcloses.html Hoth Easter Egg Contest Closes], Decipher (19 December 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990127105320/http://decipher.com/insidedecipher/archives/1997/hothcontestcloses.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Dagobah Contest (1997) ==
[[File:Decipher.com Dagobah Contest 1997 puzzle 1 page.jpg|thumb|Puzzle 1 contest page, March 1997.]]
The March 1997 Dagobah Contest posted five card-title puzzles of preview Dagobah cards.<ref name="dagobah">[http://rothko.decipher.com/new/dagobahcontest/index.html The Dagobah Contest], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327204942/http://rothko.decipher.com/new/dagobahcontest/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> Each contest page was a JPEG of four fragments of the card art and blanks for the title. Decipher added one letter a day to that JPEG.<ref name="p1">[http://rothko.decipher.com/new/dagobahcontest/puzzle1.html Puzzle 1], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327214142/http://rothko.decipher.com/new/dagobahcontest/puzzle1.html Internet Archive]</ref> Players mailed the completed title to Decipher.

After each puzzle closed, Decipher posted a solution page with a Shockwave 4-by-6 sliding-tile puzzle of the full card, including the printed title. A GIF of the card was offered for players without Shockwave.<ref name="sol1">[http://rothko.decipher.com/new/dagobahcontest/solution1.html The Dagobah Contest], Decipher (17 March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327214330/http://rothko.decipher.com/new/dagobahcontest/solution1.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="sol1b">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/diversions/theattic/dagobahcontest/solution1b.html The Dagobah Contest], Decipher (17 March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970607212621/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/diversions/theattic/dagobahcontest/solution1b.html Internet Archive]</ref> The title also appeared as HTML under the movie. A 2026 recreation of the five title puzzles and their sliding puzzles is at [https://wiki.swccg.com/preserved/dagobah-contest/ the Dagobah Contest puzzles].

Each puzzle awarded a display box of white-border Premiere packs to the first correct entry and another to a random draw from the remaining correct entries.<ref name="dagobah" /> [[Scott Randel]] of Riverside, California won the bonus prize, a display box of Dagobah, for a Puzzle Four entry mailed the morning of 17 March.<ref name="dagobah" />

== Design a Card (1997) ==
[[File:Decipher.com Design a Card contest 1997.jpg|thumb|Design a Card contest, 1997.]]
A Design a Card contest for [[Special Edition]] opened with a site announcement on 3 February 1997 and closed on 14 April 1997. Entries had to include a name, type, destiny, lore, values, game text and an image suggestion. One entry per person. The winner was to be announced in May 1997 and would receive a display box of Special Edition. The winner would not be named on the card.<ref name="dac">[http://www.decipher.com/new/cardcontest/index.html Design a Card Contest!], Decipher (1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19981206081227/http://www.decipher.com:80/new/cardcontest/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

On 23 May 1997 Decipher named [[Guy Kargl]] of Tulsa, Oklahoma the winner. His design was [[S-foils]]. Judges reviewed more than 1,000 entries. Rebel Base Leader [[Tom Lischke]] said the hardest part was narrowing that field to 12. Kargl received a display box of Special Edition. Eleven finalists each received two booster packs.<ref name="win">[http://www.decipher.com/insidedecipher/archives/1997/designawinner.html Guy Kargl Wins Star Wars CCG Card Design Contest], Rich Loftus, Decipher (23 May 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990210055006/http://www.decipher.com/insidedecipher/archives/1997/designawinner.html Internet Archive]</ref>
